title: HMD-AMP mining uncovers evolutionarily remote antimicrobial peptides with validated antibacterial activity
summary: A protein-language-model pipeline, HMD-AMP, screened host and gut-microorganism genomes from nine mammalian species and nominated antimicrobial peptides, including candidates with little similarity to known AMPs. Of 91 high-confidence peptides selected for experiments, 74 showed strong antibacterial activity and 48 were evolutionarily remote from known AMPs. Four tested peptides had broad-spectrum activity at low effective concentrations and low toxicity; the most potent reported candidate showed efficacy in a mouse peritoneal E. coli infection model.
organization: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Chinese University of Hong Kong; Hong Kong Polytechnic University; Broad Institute and collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: Of 91 high-confidence peptides selected for experiments, 74 showed strong antibacterial activity and 48 were evolutionarily remote from known AMPs.
evidence.unknown: These are in-vitro peptide activity results plus a single reported mouse peritoneal E. coli infection experiment; they do not establish human safety or efficacy, clinical antibiotic utility, or activity against every pathogen. Only 91 of the many predicted sequences were tested, and 74 showed strong activity under the authors’ assays. The entry is one paper-level finding; other AMP discovery records in this ledger use different candidate sequences, sources or design workflows. The model acronym overlaps an earlier 2021 HMD-AMP classifier preprint, but this 2026 paper is a separate study with mammalian metagenomic mining and experimental outcomes; they are not conflated.
evidence.ai_role: HMD-AMP used protein language-model representations and a hierarchical classifier to identify and rank candidate antimicrobial peptides from host and gut-microorganism metagenomic/genomic sequences. The researchers experimentally tested 91 high-confidence candidates; 74 showed strong antibacterial activity, including 48 evolutionarily remote sequences, and four had the reported broad-spectrum/low-toxicity profile. The strongest candidate was then evaluated in a mouse infection model.
